notes.meaning: Paul shares a trusted saying that wanting to be an overseer is a desire for a noble and worthwhile task. In the early church, an overseer, also called a pastor or elder, was someone who cared for the spiritual needs of a congregation. Leading God's people was not about worldly honor, but about hard, devoted work.

A church leader must live an upright life so that no one can bring a rightful charge against him. He must be faithful and pure in his marriage, self-controlled, sensible, respectable, welcoming to guests, and able to teach God's truth clearly.

differ.view: Some historic Anglican scholars teach that this rule barred any man who had married a second time after his first wife died.
Methodist teachers understand the phrase to forbid having multiple wives at once or divorcing carelessly, but not remarrying after a wife's death.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Traditional interpretations sometimes view the 'one wife' symbolically as the Church, supporting the requirement that priests remain celibate.

notes.meaning: An overseer must not drink too much wine or become loud and abusive. He cannot be quick-tempered or violent with his hands or words. Instead, he must be gentle, peaceful, and free from the love of money.

A leader must guide his own family well, leading with calm and steady dignity. His children should respect and obey him in a home marked by proper order. A father who leads well at home shows the character needed to guide a church.

Paul asks how a man who cannot manage his own household could ever take care of God's church. A local congregation is like a large spiritual family made up of brothers and sisters in Christ. If a person cannot manage the smaller family at home, he is not ready for the greater work of church leadership.

An overseer must not be someone who has only recently become a Christian. A new convert is like a young plant that has not yet grown deep roots through life's trials. Putting him into leadership too quickly could make him proud, leading to the same kind of judgment that ruined the devil.

A church leader must also have a good reputation among people outside the church. When non-believers see honesty and moral goodness in a leader, Christ is honored. If a leader has a shameful past or bad habits, Satan can trap him in disgrace and discouragement.

Deacons, who served the congregation by helping with practical needs like caring for the poor, must also meet high standards. They need to be serious, respectable, and honest in what they say. They must not drink too much wine or use their position to seek dishonest gain.

Deacons must hold firmly to the gospel, which is called a mystery because God revealed truths that human minds could not discover on their own. They must believe these truths deeply and keep a clear conscience. Their daily lives must match the holy faith they confess.

Before people are appointed as deacons, the church must examine their lives and faith. Their character and faithfulness should be tested over time. Only after they are found blameless and trustworthy should they begin serving in this office.

Paul gives moral rules for the women connected to church service, saying they must be worthy of respect. They must not spread harmful rumors or gossip about others. Instead, they should be sober-minded, self-controlled, and faithful in everything they do.

differ.view: Many Reformed teachers believe this refers to the wives of church leaders, who must support their husbands in their holy work.
Some evangelicals believe this refers to women deacons, or deaconesses, who held an official serving role in the congregation.

notes.meaning: Just like overseers, a deacon must be completely faithful to his wife. He must also be a good leader of his children and manage his household well. Loving and steady care at home shows that a person is ready to serve the church family.

Those who carry out their duties as deacons faithfully earn a respected standing among God's people. Their faithful service also brings them great confidence and bold joy in their own faith in Christ Jesus.

Paul tells Timothy that he hopes to travel to Ephesus soon to encourage him in person. Even so, he puts these guidelines into writing right away. Having written instructions would help Timothy deal with church matters without delay.

Paul writes so that if he is delayed, Timothy will know how believers should live together in God's household. The church is the family of the living God, and it holds up and displays God's truth to the world like a strong pillar.

differ.view: Reformed teachers hold that the church displays God's truth like a pillar holding up a notice, but the church does not create truth or stand above Scripture.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching views the Church as the divinely protected pillar and ground of truth that teaches with Christ's authority through the Holy Spirit.

notes.meaning: Paul quotes an early Christian confession that celebrates the wonderful truth about Jesus. Christ came in human flesh, was proven righteous by the Holy Spirit in his resurrection, was seen by angels, preached among the nations, believed on across the earth, and taken up into heavenly glory.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Modern scholars note that the oldest Greek manuscripts read 'He who appeared' rather than 'God appeared,' pointing to an early hymn about Christ.
